units: <cite ref="Mishnah Negaim 10:6">Neg. X, 6</cite> <he>וש׳ של שער וכ׳</he> and a row of hair separating them. Y. Kidd. II, 62ᵈ <he>אשה … ושי׳ של וכ׳</he> (not <he>שוטה</he>) a bald-headed woman with a row of hair going around from ear to ear. Y. Yoma IV, 41ᶜ top <he>אני ראיתיו … אלא ש׳ אחת וכ׳</he> I have seen it (the high priest’s mitre) in Rome, and there was engraved on it only in one line, ‘holy unto the Lord’. Tosef. Gitt. IX (VII), 11 <he>מלא ש׳ אחת</he> the space of one line (of writing); Y. ib. IX, 50ᶜ; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 10:1:6">Y. B. Bath. X, beg. 17ᶜ</cite>.
<cite ref="Tractate Soferim 12:8">Treat. Sof’rim XII, 8</cite>; a. fr.—Pl. <he>שִׁיטִּין</he>, <cite ref="U00752"><he>שִׁטִּ׳</he></cite> (m.), <he>שִׁיטּוֹת</he>.

Ib. שִׁיטּוֹתֶיהָ של תורה the division of lines in the Pentateuch. Ib. 9 סימן תחלת הש׳ וכ׳ the mark for the beginning of lines (in Haăzinu, Deut. XXXII) is, Haazinu, Yaʿarof &c. Y. B. Bath. l. c. מקום שני ש׳ the space of two lines; Tosef. Gitt. l. c.; Y. ib. l. c.
Ḥull. 65ᵃ בשתי תיבות פסיק להו בשני ש׳ וכ׳ written as two separate words, but not divided between two lines; a. fr.—2) (trnsf.) line of thought, opinion, principle, system.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 2:6">Lev. R. s. 2</cite> <he>אמר ש׳ אחרת</he> offered a second mode (of developing the same idea from two Scripture verses). Y. Gitt. V, 47ᶜ top; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 7:6:3">Y. Erub. VII, 24ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>ירדו לה בשִׁיטַּת וכ׳</he> they entered into (drew an analogy from) the principle laid down in the law concerning transactions of children.

<cite ref="Eruvin 99a">Erub. 99ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>מוחלפת הש׳</he>, v. <cite ref="H01098"><he>חָלַף</he></cite>; (Rashi: R. J. is at variance with his own principle, v. <cite ref="U00888"><he>שִׁיטְּתָא</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 7:1:6">Y. Pes. VII, beg. 34ᵃ</cite> <he>בשיטת ר׳ מאיר</he> following up R. Meir’s principle. Y. Peah V, 19ᵃ top [read:] <he>בשִׁיטָּתָן השיבהו בשִׁיטַּתְכֶן דאתון אמרין וכ׳</he> he (R. El.) argued against them by entering into their opinion (without adopting it for himself); according to your principle, when you say &c.; a. fr. (in Chald. diction, v. <cite ref="U00888"><he>שִׁיטְּתָא</he></cite>).—Pl. <he>שִׁיטִּין</he>.
